card.headline: Stop saying "very short"
card.sub: Say "brief" - or one of 9 other words

beats.speech: Stop saying very short. Say brief. Here are ten better words: five for a short time, and five for short texts and answers.

beats.label: a short time
beats.speech: Part 1. Five words for a short time.
Brief. It means lasting only a short time. "We had a brief phone call."
Quick. It means taking only a short time. "Let's take a quick break."

card.headline: Fleeting
card.meaning: lasting only a moment, then gone

beats.speech: Fleeting. It means lasting only a moment, then gone. "She gave me a fleeting smile."

card.headline: Momentary
card.meaning: lasting only a second or two

beats.speech: Momentary. It means lasting only a second or two. "There was a momentary silence."

card.headline: Short-lived
card.meaning: lasting a short time, often less than you hoped

beats.speech: Short-lived. It means lasting a short time, often less than you hoped. "The good weather was short-lived."

card.headline: Which word is it?
card.question: Lasting a short time, often less than you hoped: ___
card.answer: Lasting a short time, often less than you hoped: short-lived

beats.speech: Which word is it? Lasting a short time, often less than you hoped. Short-lived, or quick? | Short-lived. The good weather was short-lived.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
We had a brief phone call.
Let's take a quick break.
She gave me a fleeting smile.
There was a momentary silence.
The good weather was short-lived.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | We had a brief phone call. | Let's take a quick break. | She gave me a fleeting smile. | There was a momentary silence. | The good weather was short-lived.

beats.label: short texts and answers
beats.speech: Part 2. Five words for short texts and short answers.

card.headline: Concise
card.meaning: short and clear, with no extra words

beats.speech: Concise. It means short and clear, with no extra words. "Keep your email concise."

card.headline: Succinct
card.meaning: said clearly in very few words

beats.speech: Succinct. It means said clearly in very few words. "She gave a succinct answer."

card.headline: Terse
card.meaning: so short that it sounds unfriendly

beats.speech: Terse. It means so short that it sounds unfriendly. "He sent a terse reply."

card.headline: Snappy
card.meaning: short and clever, so it catches your attention

beats.speech: Snappy. It means short and clever, so it catches your attention. "We need a snappy title."

card.headline: Pithy
card.example: "She summed it up in one pithy sentence."

beats.speech: Pithy. It means short and full of meaning. "She summed it up in one pithy sentence."

card.headline: Which word is it?
card.question: So short that it sounds unfriendly: ___
card.answer: So short that it sounds unfriendly: terse

beats.speech: Which word is it? So short that it sounds unfriendly. Terse, or succinct? | Terse. He sent a terse reply.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
Keep your email concise.
She gave a succinct answer.
He sent a terse reply.
We need a snappy title.
She summed it up in one pithy sentence.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | Keep your email concise. | She gave a succinct answer. | He sent a terse reply. | We need a snappy title. | She summed it up in one pithy sentence.
Quick tip: whenever you need another word for any word, look it up on another word for dot net.

card.headline: Which word will you use next time?

beats.speech: That's ten words to use instead of very short. Which one will you use next time? Write it in the comments.

language_approval.notes: H58 Short long: all 10 meanings checked against OALD/Cambridge/MW senses; Abridged replaced by Pithy (abridged = shortened, not 'very short'); Quick: 'done in a short time; fast' -> 'taking only a short time' (fits 'a quick break'); Short-lived: 'ending sooner than you hoped' -> 'lasting a short time, often less than you hoped' (card, speech, quiz); Snappy: 'easy to remember' -> 'so it catches your attention'; quizzes one right answer each; American spelling; Kokoro reads short-lived as short-LIVD; caps OK
